subject.title: [Bug]: In-flight exec ignores hot tools.exec revocation

question: Should the hot runtime-config authorization checkpoint be added to the active approval-race PR, or implemented as a focused dependent follow-up after that PR lands?
rationale: Both paths can fix the security gap, but the active PR is already a large cross-platform security change; choosing whether to expand its security boundary or keep this as a narrow follow-up requires maintainer ownership of landing and review risk.

options.title: Focused dependent follow-up
options.body: Keep this issue open and land a narrow Gateway/Node runtime-policy checkpoint immediately after the approval-race foundation is merged.

options.title: Expand the active PR
options.body: Add the complete runtime-config checkpoint and its Gateway/Node race tests to the current approval-race PR before merge.

options.title: Redesign the combined boundary
options.body: Pause both paths for a broader unified authorization-plan design spanning config, approval files, and host execution.

recommendation.title: Focused dependent follow-up
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and land a narrow Gateway/Node runtime-policy checkpoint immediately after the approval-race foundation is merged.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the active related repair branch and has the strongest recent history across both Gateway and Node exec authorization paths.
